exposure: Private vs. public health insurance status
cohort: 403,642 women hospitalized for childbirth in Ireland between 2005 and 2010
finding: Women with private health insurance were significantly more likely to have various obstetric interventions, including elective and emergency cesarean delivery, operative vaginal delivery, and episiotomy, even after adjusting for obstetric risk factors.
mod_finding: Women with private coverage who had a vaginal delivery were 40% more likely to have an episiotomy compared to women with public coverage.
